findings.title: An existing work supports a focused attribution review.
findings.body: “BEND OVER ATLMIX” BI5VM7 names LUH NAE and co-writers Calen Lavon Smith and Treyvon Britt. The title, stage name and shared co-writer credit support a match to your catalog recording. The work shows 35% total known shares, with 10KCaash Publishing → Velocity Future Collections naming only Treyvon Britt in its own writer chain. No attributable claim was identified for the Luh Nae writer interest, and no recording is attached to the work. Confirm the composition, account identity and splits, then investigate the recording link and the apparent attribution gap; the 65% open remainder is not automatically yours.

findings.title: Prioritize exposure across the complete discovered catalog.
findings.body: No matching MLC work was identified for 39 reviewed recordings. The complete catalog review includes 43 recordings, with Spotify counters supplied for 18. The conservative exposure floor is 3,916,577 Spotify plays; unavailable counters are excluded, and overlapping same-title/artist versions are not added together. The per-recording streaming audit preserves every supplied counter and platform value. “Geeked Shit” has two original-delivery identifiers and a separate PLUTO remix. “GET FREAKY,” your feature with King and Dreek Jones, is now included with 1,021 visible Spotify plays; its ISRC was not returned by the catalog sources and its exact registry link remains pending. Streams do not establish your writing or ownership share.

findings.title: Use Janae Chatman to reconcile your writer identity.
findings.body: Your legal-name writer credit appears in label metadata on 33 recordings, with 5 further recordings using the stage name. The MLC LUH NAE writer line on “Bend Over” has no IPI shown. Your primary writer IPI and current PRO/MLC accounts were not established by this review. Do not create another writer identity until the existing account and all spelling/name variants have been reconciled.

findings.title: Reconcile original and alternate delivery identifiers.
findings.body: Deezer returns “Geeked Shit” under QZZ7M2635244 (Pretty Young Gangsta) and QZRD92609177 (QCLG), plus the remix under QZRD92609207. Treat these as three recording identifiers to verify, not three automatically distinct compositions. Confirm which original recordings share a composition and whether the remix adds writers, then attach the correct recordings to the verified work. Recent-release search misses can reflect ingestion or processing delays; check administrator delivery confirmations before filing. The full Chartmetric export also assigns the identical 860,870-play observation to “Bend Over (ATLMix)” QZNMT2698440 and “Bend Ova” QZLL92621679. That shared source counter is included once in the exposure floor while both ISRCs remain visible for version verification. This does not settle whether the registry works should be the same.

findings.title: A restored catalog release connects to an existing writer-name lead.
findings.body: MLC “MONEY IN THE BANK” MO1VTX names JANAE CHATMAN without an IPI and shows 50% total known shares. The visible BeatStars → Sentric claim names Benjamin Bialy in its own writer chain. The complete Chartmetric export restores “Money In The Bank,” ISRC QZPLR2585115, to the catalog. The title and legal writer name support an existing-work lead, but that recording identifier was not confirmed on the work. It is included as a composition with a recording link needing verification. Confirm the composition, writer identity and splits before any filing; the 50% open remainder is not automatically your entitlement.
